subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals \u2014 Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Cole <jordan@acmeanalytics.com>, Emily Park <emily@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals — Next Steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the context. I wanted to capture a short recap of the pain points, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level summary (what we heard)
- Pain: Hard to detect/triage model quality regressions in prod (semantic drift, hallucinations).
- Pain: No standardized evals or golden prompt sets for critical routes; ad-hoc scripts exist but not production-grade.
- Pain: Limited observability at token/route level (per-route latency percentiles, per-prompt scoring, token-cost visibility).
- Current stack: Kubernetes-based service, Datadog for infra metrics, custom evaluation scripts in a repo, vendor-hosted models for now.

Success criteria (what success looks like in a 4-week POC)
- Per-route dashboards showing latency p50/p90/p99, error rates, and a simple quality score.
- Golden prompt sets + automated nightly evals that surface regressions vs baseline.
- Tracing hooks or request identifiers to link traces to failing outputs.
- Regression alerts tied to configured thresholds and a rollout guardrail (auto-fallback to prior model or canary block).

Requested dashboards/features you asked for during the call
- Per-route latency percentiles + token-level cost breakdown.
- Top-N failure examples by route (sampled outputs).
- Regression alerting for drop in eval score or spike in hallucination rate.
- Rollout guardrails (canary + automatic rollback).

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive / POC scoping with Vivek (SE) — proposed Wed 12 Mar, 10:00 AM PT. Vivek will cover tracing hooks and eval integration.
2) Redwood to share: observability playbook + draft MA/POC plan (attached).
3) Acme to share: 1–2 golden prompt sets and an example route to instrument.
4) Security docs: we’ll send SOC2 + security questionnaire this week (cc’ing Laura for security questions).

Attachments: redwood-observability-playbook.pdf, draft-ma-plan-acme.docx

Thanks — I’ll send the calendar invite for Wed once we confirm.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Cole <jordan@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals — Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications/requests from our side:
- POC duration: we’re looking at ~4 weeks, ideally end-to-end on one high-volume route (billing-summary).
- Metrics we care most about: latency p50/p90/p99 by route, token-cost per request (so we can understand tradeoffs), and a quality score we can correlate with customer complaints.
- Stakeholders to include: Emily Park (procurement) to help with SOW/POC terms; I’ll also invite our VP Eng to the deep-dive after we lock the slot.

Also: can you share sample dashboards ahead of the call so we have a sense of layout/fields? If you can include one example of a regression alert rule that triggers an automated rollback, that’d be super helpful.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals — Next Steps

Great — thanks Jordan. Per your ask I’ve attached the playbook and a short draft MA/POC plan. Quick notes:
- We’ll prepare a sandbox dashboard set (Latency/Errors/Quality) and share a link before the deep-dive so your team can review.
- Example regression alert we’ll propose: nightly eval score delta > 5% AND increase in client-reported error rate => trigger canary block + notify on-call. We can tune thresholds during the POC.
- For tracing hooks: we’ll provide a small wrapper (library + instructions) to add request IDs to your outgoing LLM calls; that will let us join logs/traces to outputs and sample failing responses.

I’ve tentatively scheduled the technical deep-dive for Wed, 12 Mar, 10:00 AM PT — please confirm or suggest an alternate. Invite will include Vivek (SE) and Laura (security) to cover the SOC2/Q&A.

Attachments: redwood-observability-playbook.pdf, draft-ma-plan-acme.docx

Thanks — quick note from the SE side on agenda/items to prepare for the deep-dive:
- Agenda (30–45m): tracing hook design, sample golden prompt set integration, nightly eval runner, dashboard walkthrough, alerting & rollback flow.
- Can you share an example payload and one or two representative golden prompts before the call? That’ll let us pre-run a couple of evals and bring concrete examples.
- Tech note: our tracing hook is a lightweight client wrapper (Python/Node) that adds an X-Request-ID and a small context blob with route metadata; we can demo a simple Datadog/Jaeger join during the session.

I’ll also bring a short example of a regression alert rule and a canary rollback policy so we can iterate live.
